chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who bought from another man a measure of food by a known volume, then the seller said to the buyer, 'Buy this other measure from me without measuring, for it is like the one you bought.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not valid except if he measures it.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever of the foodstuffs you specify a volume for, it is not valid as an estimation (gharar). This is what is disliked from the selling of foodstuffs.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling food by estimation if it was originally sold by volume?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) rules that when selling food by volume (kayl), if a specific measure is agreed upon, selling an additional portion without measuring it out constitutes gharar (uncertainty) and is invalid. This highlights the principle that food sold by volume must be measured to avoid dispute, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on precision in commercial transactions to prevent hidden defects or disputes. The ruling underscores the distinction between fixed measures and estimated quantities, ensuring fairness in trade as derived from the Prophet's traditions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who buys some foodstuff from a man a package of a known weight. Then its owner says to the buyer, ‘Buy this other one from me without measurement, for therein is similar to what was in the other one which you have bought’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is not correct except if he measures it out’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whatever was from the foodstuffs wherein a measurement was mentioned, so it is not correct for an estimation. This is what is abhorred from selling of the foodstuffs’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

About the case of a man who buys food from another man, a package by means of known measurement then the party asks the buyer to buy from him another similar package without measurement, because it is similar to the other package already bought. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not valid without measurement.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘Venturous estimation in food items which are exchanged by measurement is not valid and it is of undesirable matters in food items.’”
